Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 99, verse 1:

(p-202) Surat al-Zalzalah (The Earthquake): its purpose is the unveiling of matters, the fullest manifestation of what has been decreed, and the division of people in recompense in the abode of permanence into happiness and misery. This is indicated by its name, when one reflects on the container and what it contains, and on what is conveyed of the wondrous decree and its vicissitudes. [It begins with] "In the name of Allah" (bismillah), who encompasses everything in power and knowledge; "the Most Merciful" (al-Rahman), who has generalized creation with His manifest blessing in oath; "the Most Compassionate" (al-Rahim), who has perfected the blessing upon His elect, in reality and in name, in essence and in form.

* *

Since He concluded the previous surah with the recompense of the righteous and the wicked in the abode of permanence according to what they had sent ahead in the places of passing away, He mentions in this one the very beginnings of that abode and the first of its ends, and He mentions in al-Qari'ah the subsequent stages of its beginnings and the last of its ends. He intensifies the warning by informing of the manifestation of what the recompense will be like, so He said, expressing it with the particle of certainty because the matter is decisive and must occur: ﴿Idha﴾ (when).

Since what causes fear is the earthquake, even if its agent is not known, and since the passive construction indicates the ease and great facility of the action, He used the passive for His saying: ﴿zuzilat al-ardu﴾ (the earth is shaken), meaning it is moved and convulsed with the quaking of resurrection after the second blast, in such a way that it engulfs all of it (p-203), not as it used to occur before that, with the shaking of some parts of it without others and in a manner less than that. The magnitude and terror of this quake are indicated by its indefiniteness, so that the soul may go in every direction in imagining it. He said, with the letter zay vowelled with a kasra because it is a verbal noun (masdar); had it been vowelled with a fatha it would have been a noun for the motion. Al-Baydawi said: "It occurs only in the doubled form."

﴿Zilzalaha﴾ (its quaking): that is, its movement and convulsion, which is fitting for it in relation to the greatness of the earth's mass and the greatness of that day. Had it been described in what befits it, the description would have been long. This is like your saying: "I honor the pious with honor, and I humiliate the wicked [the wretched] with humiliation," meaning according to what befits each.

Imam Abu Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr said: it came after Surat al-Bayyinah (The Clear Evidence) to clarify by it the attainment of the recompense of the two groups and the final destiny of the two categories mentioned in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieved among the People of the Book and the polytheists﴾ [al-Bayyinah: 6] — to His saying: ﴿Those are the worst of creation﴾ [al-Bayyinah: 6] — and His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who have believed﴾ [al-Bayyinah: 7] — to the end of the surah.

Since the outcome of that is their separation into two categories, and no definition was given of their differing states, He followed that with the final destiny of the two categories and the full accounting of the recompense of the two groups mentioned in summary, so He said, exalted is He: ﴿That Day, people will depart in scattered groups to be shown their deeds﴾ [al-Zalzalah: 6] — to the end of the surah. End.

(p-204) Since the great upheaval reveals what is hidden within what is shaken, He said: ﴿And the earth brings forth﴾, and He stated it openly rather than using a pronoun, to affirm generality, so He said: ﴿the earth﴾, that is, all of it, ﴿its burdens﴾, that is, what is buried within it, such as the dead and the treasures whose matter was heavy upon people. The word *athqal* is the plural of *thiql* (with a kasra), and this occurs when the resurrection and standing are consequent upon that bringing forth caused by that quaking, just as the bringing forth of what is in the belly, its folds and its creases, of filth, dust and other things, is consequent upon the shaking of a carpet when it is beaten. What is on its surface is a burden upon it, because God gives it the strength to bring forth all of that, just as He gave it the strength to bring forth the small, delicate, tender sprout, which is softer than silk, so that it splits the hard earth, which axes and iron cannot cut through. It also splits the date pit despite its hardness, which resists iron, so it splits into two halves and from it grows what He, glorified and exalted, wills. He splits the shell of the walnut and the almond and the peach pit and other things that are of extreme hardness, as we witness. From it emerges the tree, breaking through the earth despite its weakness and softness and the earth's hardness, and despite its being on the earth's surface, until it becomes the thickest and strongest of things. The same applies to the grain. The One who is able to do that, glorified and exalted is He, (p-205) is able to form the dead within the belly of the earth and restore them to what they were, just as the embryo is formed in the belly and forms all its openings, such as the hearing, the sight, the mouth and other things, [without] anything entering [into] that place, neither compass nor saw, and then it emerges from the belly. Likewise, the bringing forth of the dead is no different; all of it is easy for Him. Glorified is He; how great is His affair and how mighty is His authority.

When the human being sees this, he is amazed by it and does not grasp its cause, because it is a great and terrible matter that overwhelms his intellect and exceeds his capacity. [The Qur'an] expresses this by His saying: ﴿And man will say﴾, meaning this kind [of creature], which speaks truthfully about little and much, because of his forgetfulness of what the matter of the Resurrection has been confirmed to him, given his familiarity with himself and his reflection on his own disposition, out of wonder, astonishment, or bewilderment. It is also permissible that the speaker be the disbeliever, as in His saying: ﴿Who has raised us from our sleeping place?﴾ [Ya-Sin: 52], and the believer says to him: ﴿This is what the Most Merciful promised, and the messengers spoke the truth﴾ [Ya-Sin: 52]. ﴿What is the matter with it?﴾, meaning, what has happened to the earth in this affair, the like of which it has never known.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 99, verse 4:

When the discourse had been prolonged and the intent was to instill awe, the phrase that replaces "idhā" is His saying, specifying for the human being what he asked about: ﴿On that day﴾, meaning: since what was mentioned of the earthquake (p-206) and what follows from it had occurred, and it governs it. Likewise, what it is substituted for is His saying: ﴿it will relate﴾, meaning the earth, through the tongue of its state, by bringing forth what is in its belly of the dead, the treasures and other things, in a manner by which the human being knows why it was shaken and why it was brought forth, and that the warning concerning that was true.

Ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him) said: it speaks with the tongue of speech.

﴿its news﴾, meaning: those by which it was shaken and brought forth what it brought forth for their sake. And every deed done upon it is a testimony from it against those who did it, so it says: "So-and-so did such-and-such," repeated until the criminal wishes that he were driven into the Fire, so that the enumeration of that which brings shame upon him may cease. And it testifies for the believer concerning what he did, until that gladdens him. Thus everything reached by the voice of the muezzin, whether moist or dry, testifies for him.

Since it is established that nothing occurs except by His permission, the Exalted, and he (al-Biqa'i) had constructed the verbs in the passive voice (bina al-af'al li-ma lam yusamma fa'iluh, i.e., with the agent left unnamed), so that the ignorant person might not perceive who the agent of that is, he said: ﴿Because﴾, meaning, she will speak by reason of the fact that ﴿your Lord﴾, meaning the One who is good to you by establishing the truth and extinguishing falsehood to exalt your station, ﴿has inspired her﴾. He departed from the particle of termination (harf al-nihayah, i.e., "ila," "to") as a sign of hastening in the inspiration, and so he said: ﴿to her﴾, meaning, by permission to speak the aforementioned speech, by state or by utterance.

When God, exalted is He, announced the bringing forth of the burdens, among which are the dead, the longing to know the form of that bringing forth and what results from it grew intense. So He said, repeating mention of the Day for added awe: ﴿On that day﴾, i.e., since what came before, which is the time when people rise from the graves, ﴿people will issue forth﴾, i.e., return, with a return that is extremely swift and guided to the place from which they are called, so that none of them errs or goes astray from it, ﴿from their graves﴾ ﴿in scattered groups﴾ toward their Lord, who was watching over them so that He might separate them, i.e., dispersed according to their ranks in their essences and conditions: believer and disbeliever, secure and fearful, obedient and disobedient.

When He mentioned that, He followed it with its cause, saying, using the passive form in the manner of speech of those who have power: ﴿that they may be shown﴾, i.e., God will make the good-doer and the wrongdoer among them see, through whichever of His hosts He wills or without any intermediary, when He, glorified and exalted, speaks to every single one without interpreter or intermediary, as His Messenger ﷺ informed us; ﴿their deeds﴾, so that they may know their recompense; or, departing from the place of standing each to his abode, so that he may see the recompense of his deed. Then, as a consequence of that, He said, detailing the sentence that preceded it:

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 99, verse 7:

﴿Whoever does﴾ an atom's weight of good, whether a doer of good or an evildoer, Muslim or disbeliever, ﴿an atom's weight﴾, i.e., the measure of the weight of ﴿an atom﴾ of ﴿good﴾, i.e., in terms of good, ﴿will see it﴾, i.e., present, with nothing of it hidden from him, because the one who reckons (al-muhasib) has comprehensive knowledge and power. As for the disbeliever, he is made to stand upon (the fact) that it was requited to him in this world, or that it was nullified because it was built on other than the foundation of faith. So it is a form without meaning, so that his regret intensifies and his sorrow and grief grow stronger, while the believer sees it so that his joy with it increases.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 99, verse 8:

When he had mentioned good, he followed it with its opposite, saying: ﴿And whoever does an atom's weight of evil﴾, that is, whoever he may be, ﴿will see it﴾, meaning [will see] the evil from its side, ﴿and whatever is above it﴾. So the believer sees it and knows that he has been forgiven, so that his joy intensifies, while the disbeliever sees it and his grief and distress intensify. The dharra (atom, mote) is a small ant or the speck of dust that is seen floating [in the air] in the light that enters through a window opening. Its last part has returned to its first part through the reporting of news and the disclosure of secrets. It has been related in the hadith of the Bedouin that this surah comprises this final verse. Ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "It is the most judicious verse in the Qur'an." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to call it "the unique and comprehensive" (al-fadhdha al-jami'a). From the understanding (fiqh) of this, one should not belittle any sin, however small, because it accumulates with its like and becomes great, just as the Prophet (ﷺ) said to 'A'isha (may Allah be pleased with her): "Beware of belittled sins, for they have a pursuer from Allah." It is narrated, as I mentioned in my book "Masa'id al-Nazar fi'l-Ishraf 'ala Maqasid al-Suwar", in a hadith [that it is equal to half the Qur'an], and in another hadith that it is equal to a quarter of the Qur'an. There is no contradiction. The first looks at it from the standpoint that rulings are divided into rulings of this world and rulings of the Hereafter, and this surah comprises the rulings of the Hereafter in summary, and it adds to al-Qari'a by the bringing forth of burdens and that everyone sees all that he did. The second looks at it in terms of what the hadith narrated by al-Tirmidhi from 'Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) includes, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "A servant does not believe until he believes in four things: he testifies that there is no god but Allah and that I am the Messenger of Allah, who sent me with the truth; he believes in death; he believes in resurrection after death; and he believes in qadar." This hadith implies that belief in the resurrection, which this surah establishes, is a quarter of complete faith, which the Qur'an indicates. Also, the matter of religion has four parts: the matter of the Worshipped, the matter of the servants, the matter of worship, and the matter of recompense. This surah takes charge of the matter of recompense. Surah al-Kafirun is a quarter, because it concerns the matter of worship in a particular and hidden manner, although it is complete and fulfilling. Surah al-Nasr is a quarter, because it concerns the matter of worship in a general, manifest, clear and lofty manner. And Allah is the Guide to what is right, and to Him is the return.
